_meta.label: researcher-constructed illustrative exemplars
_meta.disclaimer: These Hook/Body/Close examples are written by the researcher to illustrate well-documented short-form video structure conventions (curiosity gaps, pattern interrupts, open loops, payoff, relatability) applied per genre. They are NOT transcriptions of specific real videos and should be described in the thesis as illustrative/placeholder exemplars, not scraped viral scripts. Replace any genre's set with real, transcribed high-performing Reels scripts where possible before final submission; the module works identically either way since it only needs genre-labeled Hook/Body/Close text.
_meta.schema: hook (0-3s opening line/action), body (main structure), close (CTA/payoff), principle (which short-form convention this demonstrates)

Music.hook: Wait for the beat drop at 0:03, it changes everything.
Music.body: Quick cut of humming the melody off-key, then the actual track kicks in with a perfectly timed lip-sync or instrument reveal.
Music.close: Tag someone who needs this song on their playlist.
Music.principle: open loop (promised payoff at a specific timestamp)

Music.hook: I turned a 2-star Yelp review into a song.
Music.body: Read the review dramatically, then transition into a 15-second original tune built from its exact wording.
Music.close: Comment your worst review and I'll do the next one.

Music.hook: This chord progression is illegal in 4 genres.
Music.body: Play the same 4 chords across pop, metal, lo-fi, and reggaeton versions back to back.
Music.close: Which genre hit hardest? Drop the number.
Music.principle: pattern interrupt via genre-switching, forces a choice comment

Music.hook: POV: you're the bassist everyone forgets in the group photo.
Music.body: Relatable skit of being overlooked, then a solo that proves why the bass mattered all along.
Music.close: Bassists, we see you. Follow for more slander-to-respect arcs.
Music.principle: relatability hook resolved by a competence payoff

Music.hook: Don't skip, this note will hurt your ears on purpose.
Music.body: Deliberately dissonant note held for a beat, then resolves into a satisfying chord.
Music.close: That resolution though. Full track linked in bio.
Music.principle: tension and release, curiosity through mild discomfort

Fitness.hook: You've been doing squats wrong and your knees know it.
Fitness.body: Side-by-side of the common mistake vs. the fix, with a slow-motion form breakdown.

Fitness.hook: 30 days, same time, same spot, no filter.
Fitness.body: Fast transformation montage with visible day counters, ending on day 30.
Fitness.close: Full routine in the caption, not gatekeeping this one.

Fitness.body: Demonstrate the exercise at full intensity, cut to visible fatigue at second 35.
Fitness.close: Try it and tell me at what second you gave up.
Fitness.principle: challenge framing that invites a comment-based response

Fitness.hook: My physio told me to stop doing this. I didn't listen.
Fitness.body: Show the exercise, then cut to the physio's actual reasoning with a text overlay explaining the safer alternative.
Fitness.close: Swap to this version instead, trust me.
Fitness.principle: authority tension resolved into genuine value, builds trust

Fitness.hook: Gym bro science vs. what actually works.
Fitness.body: Rapid myth-busting format: state the myth, quick beat, state the evidence-based correction.
Fitness.close: Which myth did you believe? Be honest.
Fitness.principle: myth-vs-fact structure, common in educational virality

Photography.hook: This photo took 3 seconds to shoot and 3 hours to plan.
Photography.body: Show the planning (light, angle, prop setup) sped up, then the single decisive shutter click.
Photography.close: The prep is the real work. Follow for more behind-the-scenes.
Photography.principle: reveals hidden effort behind an effortless-looking result

Photography.hook: Same subject, same phone, ₹0 vs ₹80,000 lens.
Photography.body: Split-screen comparison shot with identical framing, showing what actually changes and what doesn't.
Photography.close: Save your money, here's what to spend it on instead.

Photography.hook: Golden hour lied to you, here's the real trick.
Photography.body: Demonstrate a common lighting mistake, then the specific adjustment (white balance/angle) that fixes it.
Photography.close: Try this on your next shoot and thank me later.
Photography.principle: corrective tip framed as insider knowledge

Photography.hook: I edited this photo in under 10 seconds. Here's exactly how.
Photography.body: Screen-recorded edit with each slider adjustment labeled on screen in real time.
Photography.close: Preset link in bio if you want the shortcut.
Photography.principle: speed + full transparency of process, drives saves

Photography.hook: This is why your photos look flat and nobody tells you.
Photography.body: Show a flat, poorly-lit shot next to the same scene reshot with one compositional change.
Photography.close: One change. That's it. Comment if you want the settings.

Travel.hook: This place isn't on Google Maps yet.
Travel.body: Quick, immersive visuals of the location with directions/how-to-get-there text overlays.
Travel.close: Go before it gets discovered. Location pinned in comments.
Travel.principle: exclusivity and FOMO, rewards early discovery

Travel.hook: I spent ₹5,000 for 3 days here. Full breakdown.
Travel.body: Itemized cost overlay (stay, food, transport) synced to matching visuals of each expense.
Travel.close: Budget itinerary saved in my highlights.
Travel.principle: concrete numbers build credibility and save-worthiness

Travel.hook: Nobody warns you about this before visiting.
Travel.body: Show a common tourist mistake or scam, then the simple workaround.
Travel.close: Tag a friend who's planning this trip.
Travel.principle: protective/warning hook, drives shares to at-risk friends

Travel.hook: POV: your flight got cancelled and this happened instead.
Travel.body: Turn a travel mishap into an unexpected adventure narrative with a twist ending.
Travel.close: Worst travel disaster that turned into the best story? Comment it.
Travel.principle: narrative twist, invites story-sharing in comments

Travel.hook: This view is 10 minutes from the touristy spot everyone lines up for.
Travel.body: Show the crowded spot briefly, then cut to the quiet alternative with better visuals.
Travel.close: Skip the line, thank me later.
Travel.principle: insider alternative framing, positions viewer as in-the-know

Fashion.hook: One top, five outfits, zero new purchases.
Fashion.body: Rapid outfit-change transitions styling the same base item five different ways.
Fashion.close: Which look was your favorite? Comment the number.
Fashion.principle: versatility payoff, numbered format invites easy comments

Fashion.hook: Don't wear this color if you want to look tired.
Fashion.body: Show the unflattering combination, then the fix with a better-suited palette.
Fashion.close: Save this before your next shopping trip.

Fashion.hook: Thrifted this for ₹200, styled it like it's ₹20,000.
Fashion.body: Before (as bought) vs. after (styled) transformation with the specific styling choices called out.
Fashion.close: Thrift flips every week, follow if you want more.

Fashion.hook: The outfit formula stylists don't want you to know.
Fashion.body: Break down a repeatable formula (e.g., fitted top + relaxed bottom + one statement piece) with visual examples.
Fashion.close: Try the formula and tag me in your version.

Fashion.hook: This is why your clothes never look as good as on the model.
Fashion.body: Show the fit issue (sizing, tailoring, proportion) and the specific adjustment that fixes it.
Fashion.close: Small fix, huge difference. Save this.
Fashion.principle: single-variable fix mirrors the photography pattern, high save rate

Food.hook: This 2-ingredient hack fixes bland food instantly.
Food.body: Show the bland dish, add the two ingredients on camera, taste-test reaction at the end.
Food.close: Try it tonight and tell me it didn't work.
Food.principle: low-effort high-payoff hack, invites a challenge response

Food.hook: I made restaurant-style [dish] for less than a coffee.
Food.body: Fast-cut cooking process with cost overlay per step, ending on the plated result.
Food.close: Full recipe in the comments if you want it.
Food.principle: value/cost framing plus a comment-gated reward

Food.hook: You've been cutting onions wrong your whole life.
Food.body: Show the common technique, then the faster/safer alternative in close-up.
Food.close: Save this before your next meal prep.

Food.hook: ASMR sounds only, no talking, just this dish.
Food.body: Pure sensory cooking footage: sizzling, chopping, plating, with enhanced ambient audio.
Food.close: Sound on for the full effect. Recipe on request.
Food.principle: sensory immersion format, high watch-time via audio hook

Food.hook: This looks fancy but takes 5 minutes, I promise.
Food.body: Time-stamped quick recipe with a visible countdown overlay proving the claim.
Food.principle: credibility-proof via on-screen timer, directly answers viewer skepticism

Technology.hook: This setting has been hiding in your phone the whole time.
Technology.body: Screen-recorded walkthrough showing exactly where the setting is and what it changes.
Technology.close: Go check if you have it. Comment what you found.
Technology.principle: hidden-feature reveal, drives a verification action

Technology.hook: I tried the viral productivity app for a week. Here's what happened.
Technology.body: Day-by-day recap with a specific measurable outcome (time saved, tasks completed).
Technology.close: Worth it or not? My honest take in the caption.
Technology.principle: personal experiment narrative, builds anticipation for a verdict

Technology.hook: Stop buying this accessory, here's the free alternative.
Technology.body: Show the paid product's function, then replicate it with a built-in free feature.
Technology.close: Save yourself the money. Save this post.

Technology.hook: This AI tool did in 10 seconds what took me 2 hours.
Technology.body: Side-by-side of the manual process vs. the tool's output, timestamped.
Technology.close: Link in bio if you want to try it.
Technology.principle: dramatic time-comparison, credibility through visible timestamps

Technology.hook: Your charger is secretly ruining your battery.
Technology.body: Explain the specific habit (e.g., overnight charging) and show the simple fix.
Technology.close: Small change, longer battery life. Save this.
Technology.principle: warning + fix format, protective framing drives saves

Beauty.body: Side-by-side application and result comparison under the same lighting.
Beauty.close: Full dupe list in the comments.

Beauty.hook: Get ready with me for a meeting I'm dreading.
Beauty.body: GRWM format with routine steps intercut with commentary on the dreaded event.
Beauty.close: How do you deal with meetings like this? Comment below.
Beauty.principle: relatable narrative wrapper around a routine, invites comments

Beauty.hook: You're applying this in the wrong order and it's wasting product.
Beauty.body: Show the common (wrong) order, then the correct layering sequence with reasoning.
Beauty.close: Save this, your skin will thank you.

Beauty.hook: 24-hour wear test, no touch-ups, let's see what survives.
Beauty.body: Time-stamped check-ins across the day showing how the look holds up.
Beauty.close: Would you trust this for a full day? Comment yes or no.
Beauty.principle: proof-of-claim format via visible time progression

Beauty.hook: This is the one step everyone skips and shouldn't.
Beauty.body: Explain why the step matters with a visible before/after of skipping vs. including it.
Beauty.close: Which step do you always skip? Be honest in the comments.
Beauty.principle: confession-inviting hook, normalizes engagement via shared habit

Lifestyle.hook: My 5am routine that actually stuck for 100 days.
Lifestyle.body: Fast montage of each routine step with a day-counter overlay building credibility.
Lifestyle.close: Full routine breakdown in my highlights.
Lifestyle.principle: consistency-proof via visible counter, aspirational but concrete

Lifestyle.hook: The productivity hack that felt fake until I tried it.
Lifestyle.body: Skeptical setup, then a real before/after of the day's output using the hack.
Lifestyle.close: Try it for 3 days and report back.
Lifestyle.principle: skepticism-to-belief arc, invites a personal challenge

Lifestyle.hook: A day in my life when everything goes wrong.
Lifestyle.body: Chronological mishaps shot in real time with dry-humor captions.
Lifestyle.close: Tell me your worst day-in-the-life moment.
Lifestyle.principle: relatable chaos narrative, low production pressure, high shareability

Lifestyle.hook: I decluttered my whole room and found this.
Lifestyle.body: Time-lapse of the declutter process ending on an unexpected or funny find.
Lifestyle.close: What's the weirdest thing you've found decluttering?
Lifestyle.principle: curiosity payoff plus a comment-inviting question

Lifestyle.hook: Things I stopped doing in my 20s that changed everything.
Lifestyle.body: Numbered list format, each item shown with a quick visual and one-line reasoning.
Lifestyle.close: Which one resonates most? Comment the number.
Lifestyle.principle: listicle format, easy to scan and comment on a single item

Comedy.body: Absurd escalating skit of an overactive imagination spiraling from a normal thought.
Comedy.close: Tag someone whose brain does this too.

Comedy.hook: POV: you're the friend who always says 'just one more episode'.
Comedy.body: Exaggerated skit of the lie escalating across a full night, ending in sunrise.
Comedy.close: We've all been this friend. Comment if it's you.

Comedy.hook: Rating restaurant bathroom soaps like it's my job.
Comedy.body: Deadpan, mock-serious review format applied to something trivial, escalating absurdity.
Comedy.close: Follow for more reviews nobody asked for.
Comedy.principle: mock-seriousness on a low-stakes topic, novelty humor

Comedy.hook: When the WiFi buffers during the most important scene.
Comedy.body: Physical comedy reaction escalating from mild annoyance to full despair.
Comedy.close: The pain is universal. Tag your WiFi's victim.

Comedy.hook: Explaining my job to my grandparents, a tragedy in 3 acts.
Comedy.body: Three escalating attempts to explain a modern job to a confused older relative, each funnier than the last.
Comedy.close: How did that conversation go for you? Comment below.
